newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices gain again with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices gain again with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly moved higher again Tuesday in moderate trade, boosted by another rally in crude and still-tight East Coast supplies, industry sources said.

"It's still a pretty tight market across the board. Oil prices may be in the stratosphere, but there's not a lot of supply out there," said one cash trader, noting firmer crude also lent support to resid.
At the U.S. Gulf, high sulphurs led the way up, with three percent gaining 50 cents or more to $20.50 a barrel on reports 40,000 prompt barrels sold at $20.75 (FOB Beaumont, Texas).
USG one percent saw similar gains to about $20.50.
Traders said a Florida utility tender for 110,000 barrels of 1.8 percent material was awarded at $21.90 (delivered).
In New York Harbor, one percent climbed almost 50 cents to $21.25, with November paper quoted early in the $21.10-35 area but likely higher later with crude.
NYH high sulphurs notionally firmed by 25-50 cents, with 2.2 percent now pegged on either side of $19.75, traders said.
New York City gate gas prices held steady Tuesday in the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
